Many phones stop apps in the background to save battery. That can make Rave miss steps and reminders. Two minutes here fixes it.
Battery optimisation is off for Rave
Android won\'t restrict Rave. Also check your phone\'s own settings below.
Rave can be stopped in the background
Set Rave to \"Unrestricted\" / \"Don\'t optimise\" so steps keep counting.
Steps are counted by your phone\'s step sensor, which uses almost no battery. These settings only let Rave read it regularly.
1. App settings → Battery saver → No restrictions.\n2. Turn on Autostart for Rave (button below).\n3. Open Recent apps, long-press Rave and tap the lock icon.

1. App settings → Battery → Unrestricted.\n2. Settings → Battery → Background usage limits: remove Rave from Sleeping and Deep sleeping apps.\n3. Turn off \"Put unused apps to sleep\" or add Rave to Never sleeping apps.
1. App settings → Battery usage → allow Background activity and Auto launch.\n2. Battery → More settings: turn off \"Optimise battery use\" for Rave.\n3. Lock Rave in Recent apps.
1. Settings → Battery → Background power consumption: allow Rave.\n2. i Manager → App manager → Autostart: turn on Rave.\n3. Lock Rave in Recent apps.
1. Phone Master → App launch / Auto-start: turn on Rave.\n2. App settings → Battery → turn off Power saving for Rave.\n3. Lock Rave in Recent apps.
1. Settings → Battery → App launch: set Rave to Manage manually and allow all three.\n2. Lock Rave in Recent apps.
1. App settings → Battery → Unrestricted (or Don\'t optimise).\n2. Allow background activity if your phone has that option.

Physical activity access lets Rave notice when you start walking, so it can offer to log it. Nothing is recorded until you agree.
To measure a detected walk while the app is closed, choose “Allow all the time” on the next screen. Location is only used during a detected walk.
The camera is used to scan barcodes, nutrition labels and meals. Photos stay on your phone, except meal photos, which are sent to Google Gemini for recognition.
The camera is used only to scan a friend\'s invite QR code. No photos are taken or stored.
Numbers are hashed on your phone and only the hashes are compared. Your contacts are never uploaded.
